text: The internet ran out of addresses in twenty eleven.
Every device online needs an I P address.
The original system, I P version four, uses thirty-two bits.
That's about four point three billion addresses.
Sounds like a lot, until there are more phones than people.
In twenty eleven, the central pool handed out its last blocks.
So your whole home shares one public address.
Your router keeps track of who asked for what.
The real fix is I P version six, with a hundred and twenty-eight bits.
Enough for every grain of sand on Earth, many times over.
